active-hang: Grab a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands just wider than your shoulders, and hang with straight arms.
Pull your shoulder blades down and slightly back, so your body rises a little without bending your elbows.
Hold that engaged position with your legs still and your core tight.
Breathe steadily for the whole hold, then lower down under control.
archer-push-up: Start in a push-up position with your hands much wider than your shoulders.
Lower your chest toward one hand, bending that elbow while the other arm stays nearly straight and slides out to the side.
Push back up to the middle, then lower toward the other hand.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels throughout.
assault-bike: Sit on the bike, set the seat so your knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke, and hold the handles.
Push and pull the handles while you pedal, so arms and legs drive the fan together.
Keep your chest up and your core braced; go at an even pace or in hard intervals.
Slow down gradually at the end instead of stopping abruptly.
assisted-chin-up: Set the assistance weight (more weight means more help) and kneel or stand on the platform.
Grab the handles with your palms facing you, about shoulder-width apart, and hang with straight arms.
Pull yourself up until your chin passes the handles, squeezing your biceps and back.
Lower yourself slowly until your arms are straight again.
assisted-pistol-squat: Stand on one leg next to a post, doorframe or suspension strap and hold on lightly with one or both hands.
Stretch the other leg out in front of you.
Sit down on the standing leg as far as you can control, keeping the heel down and the knee in line with your toes.
Push back up to standing, using your hands only as much as you need.
assisted-pull-up: Set the assistance weight (more weight means more help) and kneel or stand on the platform.
Grab the handles with an overhand grip, a little wider than your shoulders, and hang with straight arms.
Pull yourself up by driving your elbows down until your chin passes the handles.
Lower yourself slowly until your arms are straight again.
banded-clamshell: Put a band around your legs just above the knees and lie on your side with your hips and knees bent and your feet together.
Rest your head on your lower arm and keep your hips stacked.
Keeping your feet together, open your top knee as far as you can without rolling your hips back.
Close the knee slowly against the band's pull and repeat, then switch sides.
banded-dead-bug: Lie on your back holding a band anchored behind your head, arms straight up above your chest, with tension in the band.
Lift your legs so your hips and knees are bent at 90 degrees, and press your lower back into the floor.
Slowly extend one leg until it hovers just above the floor while your arms keep the band still.
Bring the leg back and repeat with the other leg, keeping your lower back flat the whole time.
banded-donkey-kick: Get on your hands and knees with a band looped around your feet or just above your knees.
Keeping the knee bent at 90 degrees, kick one foot up toward the ceiling by squeezing your glute.
Stop before your lower back arches, pause, and lower slowly.
Finish your reps and switch legs.
banded-face-pull: Anchor a band at about face height and hold one end in each hand with your palms facing down.
Step back until there is tension, with your arms straight in front of you.
Pull the band toward your face, leading with your elbows high and spreading your hands apart.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end, then return slowly.
banded-fire-hydrant: Get on your hands and knees with a band just above your knees.
Keeping the knee bent, lift one leg out to the side as high as you can without tilting your hips.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly.
Finish your reps and switch sides.
banded-frog-pump: Lie on your back with a band above your knees, the soles of your feet together and your knees falling open.
Pull your heels close to your hips and rest your arms on the floor.
Drive through the outside edges of your feet to lift your hips, squeezing your glutes and pushing your knees out against the band.
Lower your hips slowly and repeat.
banded-glute-bridge: Lie on your back with a band just above your knees, knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart.
Push your knees slightly out against the band.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower slowly.
banded-hip-thrust: Sit with your upper back against a bench, a band above your knees and your feet flat, hip-width apart.
Keep your chin tucked and your knees pushed slightly out against the band.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your thighs and torso are level.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower under control.
banded-kickback: Loop a band around one ankle and anchor the other end low in front of you, or loop it around both feet.
Stand tall holding a support, with a slight bend in your standing knee.
Push the working leg straight back by squeezing your glute, without arching your lower back.
Return slowly, finish your reps and switch legs.
banded-lat-pulldown: Anchor a band high overhead and kneel or sit below it, holding one end in each hand with straight arms.
Pull your shoulders down, then drive your elbows down toward your ribs.
Squeeze your lats at the bottom with your chest up.
Let your arms rise slowly back to the start.
banded-lateral-walk: Put a band just above your knees or around your ankles and stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Bend your knees slightly and sit your hips back into a quarter squat.
Step sideways, keeping tension in the band and your toes pointing forward.
Take the same number of steps back the other way.
banded-pallof-press: Anchor a band at chest height and stand side-on to it, holding the end with both hands at your chest.
Step away until there is tension and stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees soft.
Press your hands straight out in front of you without letting your torso turn toward the anchor.
Hold for a moment, bring your hands back to your chest, and switch sides after your reps.
banded-row: Anchor a band at chest height and hold one end in each hand, arms straight in front of you.
Step back until there is tension, stand tall with your knees soft.
Pull your hands toward your ribs, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Return slowly until your arms are straight again.
banded-seated-hip-abduction: Sit on the edge of a bench or chair with a band just above your knees and your feet flat.
Lean forward slightly with a straight back.
Push your knees apart against the band as far as you can.
Pause, then let your knees come back together slowly.
banded-squat: Stand on a band with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the other end at your shoulders, or wear it just above your knees.
Brace your core and push your hips back as you bend your knees.
Squat down until your thighs are about parallel to the floor, keeping your knees in line with your toes.
Drive through your whole foot to stand back up.
banded-standing-hip-abduction: Stand with a band around your ankles or just above your knees, holding a support if you like.
Shift your weight onto one leg and keep your torso upright.
Lift the other leg out to the side without leaning, leading with your heel.
Lower slowly, finish your reps and switch legs.
banded-woodchop: Anchor a band high on one side and hold the end with both hands, arms nearly straight.
Stand side-on with your feet wider than your shoulders.
Pull the band diagonally down and across your body, turning your hips and pivoting on your back foot.
Return slowly along the same path, finish your reps and switch sides.
battle-ropes: Hold one rope end in each hand, stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and sit into a quarter squat.
Keep your chest up and your core braced.
Move your arms up and down fast to send waves along the ropes, alternating or together.
Work in timed intervals and keep breathing.
bear-crawl: Start on your hands and knees, then lift your knees an inch off the floor with your back flat.
Move one hand and the opposite foot forward at the same time.
Keep your hips low and level and your knees just above the floor.
Crawl forward (or backward) for the set distance or time.
bear-plank: Start on your hands and knees with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Brace your core and lift your knees an inch off the floor.
Hold with a flat back and steady breathing.
Lower your knees back down to finish.
belt-squat: Attach the belt around your hips, stand on the platform with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the handles.
Release the stopper so the load hangs from your hips.
Squat down by bending your knees and hips until your thighs are about parallel, keeping your chest up.
Drive through your feet to stand back up, and lock the stopper when you're done.
bent-over-rear-delt-raise: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and hinge at your hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, knees soft.
Let the weights hang below your chest with your palms facing each other and a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms out to the sides until they are level with your body, squeezing your rear shoulders.
bird-dog: Start on your hands and knees with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Brace your core and keep your back flat.
Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with your torso.
Hold for a moment, return, and repeat with the other arm and leg.
bulgarian-split-squat: Stand a stride in front of a bench, holding dumbbells at your sides, and rest the top of your back foot on the bench.
Keep your chest up and most of your weight on the front foot.
Lower your back knee toward the floor until your front thigh is about parallel to it.
Drive through the front heel to stand back up; finish your reps and switch legs.
burpee: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down, place your hands on the floor and jump your feet back into a push-up position.
Do a push-up (optional), then jump your feet back toward your hands.
Jump up with your arms overhead and land softly to start the next rep.
butterfly-stretch: Sit on the floor with the soles of your feet together and your knees falling out to the sides.
Hold your feet and sit tall.
Gently lower your knees toward the floor, or lean forward from your hips, until you feel a stretch in your inner thighs.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing slowly; don't bounce.
cable-pallof-hold: Set a cable at chest height, stand side-on to it and hold the handle with both hands at your chest.
Step away until there is tension, feet shoulder-width apart and knees soft.
Press the handle straight out and hold it there, not letting the cable turn your torso.
Breathe steadily through the hold, then switch sides.
cable-standing-hip-abduction: Attach an ankle strap to a low cable and put it on the ankle farthest from the machine.
Stand side-on to the machine, holding it for balance, with your standing knee soft.
Lift the strapped leg out to the side without leaning your torso.
Lower slowly, finish your reps and switch legs.
cable-woodchop: Set a cable high on one side, hold the handle with both hands and stand side-on with feet wider than your shoulders.
Pull the handle diagonally down and across your body to the opposite hip, turning your hips and pivoting your back foot.
Return slowly along the same path, finish your reps and switch sides.
calf-raise: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a wall for balance if needed; stand on a step edge for more range.
Rise onto the balls of your feet as high as you can.
Pause at the top, squeezing your calves.
Lower your heels slowly and repeat.
captains-chair-knee-raise: Stand in the captain's chair, rest your forearms on the pads and grip the handles, back against the pad.
Let your legs hang straight down.
Raise your knees toward your chest by curling your hips up, without swinging.
Lower your legs slowly and repeat.
chair-dip: Sit on the edge of a sturdy chair or bench, hands next to your hips, fingers pointing forward.
Slide your hips off the edge with your legs bent (or straight for more difficulty).
Lower yourself by bending your elbows until they reach about 90 degrees, keeping your back close to the chair.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
chest-supported-row: Set the chest pad so the handles are just within reach, then sit or lie with your chest firmly against it.
Grip the handles with straight arms.
Pull the handles toward your ribs, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Return slowly until your arms are straight again, keeping your chest on the pad.
clamshell: Lie on your side with your hips and knees bent and your feet together.
Rest your head on your lower arm and keep your hips stacked.
Keeping your feet together, open your top knee as far as you can without rolling your hips back.
Close it slowly and repeat, then switch sides.
commando-pull-up: Stand beneath a pull-up bar, side-on, and grab it with both hands close together, one in front of the other.
Pull yourself up so your head passes to one side of the bar.
Lower slowly and alternate sides with each rep.
copenhagen-plank: Lie on your side and rest your top foot (or knee, for an easier version) on a bench, the bottom leg underneath it.
Prop yourself up on your forearm with your elbow under your shoulder.
Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line, supported by your top leg's inner thigh.
Hold with steady breathing, then switch sides.
cossack-squat: Stand with your feet very wide, toes turned slightly out.
Shift your weight to one side and squat down on that leg, while the other leg straightens with the toes pointing up.
Keep your chest up and the heel of the bent leg down.
Push back to the middle and repeat on the other side.
crab-walk: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat, and place your hands behind you, fingers pointing toward your feet.
Lift your hips off the floor.
Walk forward or backward on your hands and feet, keeping your hips up.
Keep going for the set distance or time.
curtsy-lunge: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Step one foot diagonally back behind the other, as if curtsying.
Bend both knees until your front thigh is about parallel to the floor, keeping your chest up and front knee over your toes.
Push through the front heel to return, and alternate legs.
dead-hang: Grab a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Lift your feet and hang with straight arms and relaxed shoulders.
Keep your body still and breathe steadily.
Hold as long as you can keep a firm grip, then step down.
decline-sit-up: Hook your feet under the pads of a decline bench and lie back with your knees bent.
Cross your arms over your chest or hold your hands beside your head without pulling on it.
Curl your torso up until you're sitting upright.
deficit-reverse-lunge: Stand on a low step or plate holding dumbbells at your sides.
Step one foot back off the step to the floor.
Lower your back knee toward the floor until your front thigh is about parallel, chest up.
Drive through the front heel to step back up, and alternate legs or finish one side first.
donkey-kick: Get on your hands and knees with a flat back.
Keeping the knee bent at 90 degrees, kick one foot up toward the ceiling by squeezing your glute.
Stop before your lower back arches, pause, and lower slowly.
Finish your reps and switch legs.
doorway-chest-stretch: Stand in a doorway and place your forearms on the frame, elbows at about shoulder height.
Step one foot forward through the doorway.
Lean gently forward until you feel a stretch across your chest and the front of your shoulders.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing slowly.
doorway-row: Stand in an open doorway, grab both sides of the frame at chest height and bring your feet close to the threshold.
Lean back until your arms are straight, keeping your body in a straight line.
Pull your chest toward the doorway by squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower yourself back slowly. Make sure the frame is sturdy first.
dragon-flag: Lie on a bench and grip it behind your head.
Lift your whole body up so you're resting on your upper back, legs and hips in a straight line pointing up.
Lower your body slowly as one straight unit, without bending at the hips.
Stop before your lower back arches, then raise back up. Start with small ranges.
dumbbell-curtsy-lunge: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Step one foot diagonally back behind the other, as if curtsying.
Bend both knees until your front thigh is about parallel to the floor, chest up.
Push through the front heel to return, and alternate legs.
dumbbell-glute-bridge: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, and rest a dumbbell across your hips, holding it in place.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes at the top.
dumbbell-hip-thrust: Sit with your upper back against a bench and a dumbbell resting on your hips, feet flat and hip-width apart.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your thighs and torso are level.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower under control.
dumbbell-lateral-lunge: Hold a dumbbell in each hand (or one at your chest) and stand with your feet together.
Take a wide step out to the side.
Sit back into that hip, bending the stepping knee while keeping the other leg straight and both feet flat.
Push off to return to the start, and alternate sides.
dumbbell-skull-crusher: Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms straight above your chest and palms facing each other.
Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells beside your head.
Straighten your arms to lift them back up.
dumbbell-sumo-deadlift: Stand with your feet wide and toes turned out, holding one dumbbell by its end between your legs.
Push your hips back and bend your knees, keeping your back flat and chest up, until the dumbbell nears the floor.
Drive through your heels to stand up tall, squeezing your glutes.
explosive-push-up: Start in a push-up position with your hands just wider than your shoulders.
Lower your chest toward the floor.
Push up hard enough that your hands leave the floor.
Land softly with bent elbows and go straight into the next rep.
fast-feet: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, knees bent and weight on the balls of your feet.
Run in place as fast as you can with short, quick steps.
Keep your chest up and your arms pumping.
feet-elevated-pike-push-up: Put your feet on a bench or box and your hands on the floor, then walk your hands back so your hips are high and your body forms an upside-down V.
Keep your arms and legs straight and your head between your arms.
Bend your elbows to lower the top of your head toward the floor.
Press back up to straight arms.
fire-hydrant: Get on your hands and knees with a flat back.
Keeping the knee bent, lift one leg out to the side as high as you can without tilting your hips.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly.
Finish your reps and switch sides.
forward-lunge: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Take a big step forward and lower your back knee toward the floor until both knees are at about 90 degrees.
Keep your chest up and your front knee over your toes.
Push through the front heel to step back, and alternate legs.
frog-pump: Lie on your back with the soles of your feet together and your knees falling open, heels close to your hips.
Rest your arms on the floor.
Drive through the outside edges of your feet to lift your hips, squeezing your glutes.
Lower your hips slowly and repeat.
front-foot-elevated-split-squat: Place your front foot on a low step or plate and your back foot a stride behind, holding dumbbells at your sides.
Keep your chest up and most of your weight on the front foot.
Lower your back knee toward the floor, going deeper than a normal split squat.
Drive through the front heel to stand back up; finish your reps and switch legs.
glute-bridge-march: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, and lift your hips into a bridge.
Keeping your hips high and level, lift one foot a few inches off the floor.
Put it down and lift the other foot.
Keep marching without letting your hips drop or rotate.
glute-focused-back-extension: Set up on a back extension bench with the pad just below your hips and turn your toes slightly out.
Round your upper back slightly and cross your arms over your chest.
Lower your torso by bending at the hips, then raise it by squeezing your glutes, stopping when your body is in a straight line.
Don't overextend your lower back at the top.
half-burpee: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down, place your hands on the floor and jump your feet back into a plank.
Jump your feet back toward your hands.
Stand up and repeat; there's no push-up or jump.
half-kneeling-pallof-press: Set a cable at chest height and kneel side-on to it on the knee closest to the machine, the other foot in front.
Hold the handle with both hands at your chest, with tension in the cable.
Press the handle straight out without letting your torso turn toward the machine.
Bring it back to your chest, finish your reps and switch sides.
hanging-knee-raise: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip and straight arms.
Brace your core to stop any swinging.
Raise your knees toward your chest by curling your hips up.
Lower your legs slowly and repeat.
heel-elevated-goblet-squat: Place your heels on a small plate or wedge, feet shoulder-width apart, and hold a dumbbell vertically at your chest.
Keep your chest up and elbows inside your knees.
Squat down as deep as you can while staying upright, knees travelling forward over your toes.
Drive through your feet to stand back up.
heel-tap: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, arms by your sides.
Lift your head and shoulders slightly off the floor.
Reach one hand toward the heel on the same side by bending sideways, then the other.
Keep alternating without letting your shoulders drop.
high-knees: Stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Run in place, driving your knees up to about hip height.
Land on the balls of your feet and pump your arms.
Keep a quick pace for the set time.
hiking: Wear supportive shoes and pick a trail that suits your fitness.
Walk at a steady pace, taking shorter steps on steep parts.
Keep an upright posture and use your arms (or poles) on the climbs.
Bring water and take breaks as needed.
hindu-push-up: Start in a downward-dog position: hands and feet on the floor, hips high, arms and legs straight.
Bend your elbows and swoop your chest down and forward close to the floor.
Continue forward and up until your arms are straight and your chest is lifted, hips low.
Push your hips back up to return to the start.
hip-abduction-machine: Sit in the machine with your back against the pad and the pads on the outside of your knees.
Push your knees outward as far as you comfortably can.
Let them come back together slowly without the weights touching down.
hip-adduction-machine: Sit in the machine with your back against the pad and the pads on the inside of your knees, legs apart.
Let them open again slowly without the weights touching down.
hip-airplane: Stand on one leg and hinge forward until your torso and back leg are about parallel to the floor; hold a support if needed.
Keep your standing knee slightly bent.
Rotate your hips and torso open toward the ceiling, then close them back toward the floor.
Move slowly and under control, then switch legs.
hollow-body-hold: Lie on your back with your arms overhead and legs straight.
Press your lower back into the floor.
Lift your shoulders, arms and legs a few inches off the floor, making a shallow banana shape.
Hold with steady breathing; bend your knees to make it easier.
hollow-rock: Get into a hollow body hold: lower back pressed down, shoulders, arms and legs lifted.
Rock back and forth from your upper back to your hips.
Stop if your lower back lifts off or your shape breaks.
jumping-jack: Stand with your feet together and arms by your sides.
Jump your feet out wide while raising your arms overhead.
Jump back to feet together and arms down.
Keep a steady rhythm, landing softly on the balls of your feet.
kettlebell-romanian-deadlift: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a kettlebell by the handle in front of your thighs.
Keep a slight bend in your knees and your back flat.
Push your hips back and lower the kettlebell along your legs until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to stand back up, squeezing your glutes.
knee-push-up: Start on your hands and knees, then walk your hands forward so your body is in a straight line from head to knees.
Place your hands just wider than your shoulders.
Lower your chest toward the floor, elbows at about 45 degrees from your body.
Push back up to straight arms.
l-sit-hold: Sit between two parallel bars or low boxes (or on the floor) with your hands next to your hips.
Press down to lift your hips off the ground with straight arms.
Raise your straight legs so they're level with the floor (bend your knees to make it easier).
Hold with your shoulders pushed down, then lower.
l-sit-pull-up: Hang from a pull-up bar and raise your straight legs in front of you until they're level with the floor.
Keep your legs up for the whole set.
Pull yourself up until your chin passes the bar.
Lower slowly with your legs still raised.
landmine-press: Set one end of a barbell in a landmine holder or a corner, and hold the other end at your shoulder with one or both hands.
Stand in a staggered stance with your core braced.
Press the bar up and forward until your arm is straight.
Lower it back to your shoulder under control.
landmine-romanian-deadlift: Set one end of a barbell in a landmine holder and stand facing the other end, holding it with both hands near the plates.
Keep a slight bend in your knees and your back flat.
Push your hips back and lower the bar until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to stand back up.
landmine-squat: Set one end of a barbell in a landmine holder and hold the other end at your chest with both hands.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, leaning slightly into the bar.
Squat down until your thighs are about parallel to the floor, chest up.
Drive through your feet to stand back up.
lat-pulldown: Sit at the pulldown machine with your thighs under the pads and grab the bar a little wider than your shoulders.
Lean back slightly with your chest up.
Pull the bar down to your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back.
Let the bar rise slowly until your arms are straight.
lateral-lunge: Take a wide step out to the side.
Sit back into that hip, bending the stepping knee while keeping the other leg straight and both feet flat.
Push off to return to the start, and alternate sides.
lateral-shuffle: Stand in an athletic stance: feet shoulder-width apart, knees bent, hips back.
Shuffle sideways with quick steps, without crossing your feet or bringing them together.
Change direction after a few steps or at the end of your space.
leg-curl: Set up in the leg curl machine with the pad just above your heels and your knees in line with the machine's pivot.
Curl your heels toward your hips as far as you can.
Lower slowly without letting the weight stack touch down.
leg-swings-stretch: Stand next to a wall or post and hold it for balance.
Swing your outside leg forward and back in a relaxed, controlled arc.
Let the swings get a little bigger as you loosen up.
Do the same side to side in front of your body, then switch legs.
lying-hamstring-walkout: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, and lift your hips into a bridge.
Keeping your hips up, walk your heels out in small steps until your legs are nearly straight.
Walk them back in to the start.
Keep your hips high the whole time.
machine-lateral-raise: Sit in the machine with the pads against the outside of your upper arms and hold the handles.
Keep your back against the pad.
Raise your arms out to the sides until they're level with your shoulders.
meadows-row: Set one end of a barbell in a landmine holder or corner and stand side-on to the other end in a staggered stance.
Hinge forward and grab the end of the bar with an overhand grip, resting your other forearm on your knee.
Row the bar up toward your hip, driving your elbow back.
Lower it slowly with your back flat, then switch sides.
negative-pull-up: Use a box or jump to get your chin above a pull-up bar, holding it with an overhand grip.
Take your feet off the support.
Lower yourself as slowly as you can, taking 3 to 5 seconds, until your arms are straight.
neutral-grip-pull-up: Grab the parallel handles of a pull-up station with your palms facing each other.
Pull yourself up until your chin passes the handles, driving your elbows down.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
nordic-hamstring-curl: Kneel on a padded surface with your ankles anchored under something solid, or held by a partner.
Keep your body in a straight line from knees to head, hands ready in front of your chest.
Lower your body forward as slowly as you can, resisting with your hamstrings.
Catch yourself with your hands at the bottom and push back up. Start with small ranges.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Swings: Stand with your feet a little wider than your shoulders, a kettlebell on the floor just in front of you.
Hinge at the hips, grab the handle and hike the kettlebell back between your legs.
Snap your hips forward to swing it up to about chest height, arms straight and relaxed.
Let it fall back between your legs, hinging again, and flow into the next swing. Keep your back flat throughout.
pendlay-row: Stand over a barbell on the floor with your feet hip-width apart.
Hinge until your torso is almost parallel to the floor and grab the bar a little wider than your shoulders, back flat.
Pull the bar explosively to your lower chest.
Lower it back to the floor, letting it come to a full stop before each rep.
pike-push-up: Start in a push-up position, then walk your feet in so your hips are high and your body forms an upside-down V.
Keep your arms and legs straight and your head between your arms.
Bend your elbows to lower the top of your head toward the floor.
Press back up to straight arms.
pistol-squat: Stand on one leg with the other leg straight in front of you, arms forward for balance.
Sit down on the standing leg as low as you can while keeping the heel down.
Keep the free leg off the floor and your chest up.
Drive through your standing foot to rise back up, then switch legs.
plank-jack: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and your feet together.
Jump your feet out wide, then back together.
Keep your hips level and your core braced throughout.
Keep a steady rhythm for the set time.
plank-shoulder-tap: Start in a high plank with your feet a little wider than your hips.
Lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder.
Put the hand back down and tap with the other.
Keep your hips as still as possible; widen your feet to make it easier.
prone-t-raise: Lie face down with your arms out to the sides in a T, thumbs pointing up.
Rest your forehead on a towel.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together to lift your arms a few inches off the floor.
prone-y-raise: Lie face down with your arms overhead in a Y shape, thumbs pointing up.
Rest your forehead on a towel.
Lift your arms a few inches off the floor by drawing your shoulder blades down and back.
push-up-shoulder-tap: Start in a push-up position with your feet a little wider than your hips.
At the top, tap one hand to the opposite shoulder, then the other.
Keep your hips as still as possible and repeat.
Push_Press: Hold a barbell on the front of your shoulders with your hands just wider than shoulder-width, feet hip-width apart.
Dip by bending your knees slightly, keeping your torso upright.
Drive up through your legs and use that momentum to press the bar overhead until your arms are straight.
Lower the bar back to your shoulders under control.
reverse-snow-angel: Lie face down with your arms by your sides, palms down, and your forehead resting on a towel.
Lift your arms slightly off the floor.
Sweep them in a wide arc out to the sides and overhead, then back down to your hips.
Keep your arms off the floor for the whole set.
scapular-push-up: Start in a high plank with straight arms.
Without bending your elbows, let your chest sink so your shoulder blades come together.
Push the floor away so your shoulder blades spread apart and your upper back rounds slightly.
Repeat slowly, moving only at your shoulder blades.
seal-jack: Stand with your feet together and your arms straight out in front of you, palms together.
Jump your feet out wide while opening your arms out to the sides.
Jump back to the start, clapping your hands together in front.
seated-forward-fold-stretch: Sit on the floor with your legs straight in front of you.
Sit tall, then hinge forward from your hips, reaching toward your feet.
Keep your back as long as you can; bend your knees slightly if needed.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing slowly.
shrimp-squat: Stand on one leg and bend the other knee so you can hold that foot behind you.
Reach your free arm forward for balance.
Lower yourself until the knee of the held leg gently touches the floor.
Drive through your standing foot to rise back up, then switch legs.
side-lying-hip-abduction: Lie on your side with your legs straight and stacked, head resting on your lower arm.
Lift your top leg toward the ceiling, leading with your heel and toes pointing forward.
Stop before your hips roll back.
Lower slowly, finish your reps and switch sides.
side-plank-hip-dip: Get into a side plank on your forearm, elbow under your shoulder and feet stacked.
Lower your hips toward the floor without touching it.
Lift them back up past the straight line.
Finish your reps, then switch sides.
Side_Bridge: Lie on your side with your forearm on the floor, elbow under your shoulder, and your legs straight and stacked.
Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from head to feet.
Hold without letting your hips sag.
single-dumbbell-skullcrusher: Lie on a flat bench holding one dumbbell with both hands, arms straight above your chest.
Keep your upper arms still and pointing up.
Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell toward your forehead.
Straighten your arms to lift it back up.
single-leg-calf-raise: Stand on one foot, holding a wall for balance; stand on a step edge for more range.
Rise onto the ball of your foot as high as you can.
Pause at the top, squeezing your calf.
Lower slowly, finish your reps and switch feet.
single-leg-romanian-deadlift: Stand on one leg holding a dumbbell in the opposite hand, standing knee slightly bent.
Hinge forward at the hip, letting the free leg rise behind you, until your torso is nearly level with the floor.
Keep your back flat and your hips square to the floor.
Drive back up to standing by squeezing your glute; switch sides after your reps.
sissy-squat: Stand tall holding a support with one hand, feet hip-width apart.
Rise onto the balls of your feet and lean back as you bend your knees forward.
Keep a straight line from your knees to your head and lower as far as you can control.
Push back up through your quads to stand.
skater-hop: Stand on one leg with a slight bend in your knee.
Jump sideways onto the other leg, landing softly with a bent knee.
Swing the free leg behind you and your arms across your body for balance.
Hop back to the other side and keep alternating.
skater-squat: Stand on one leg with your arms reaching forward for balance.
Bend the standing knee and lower the other knee toward the floor behind you, the free foot off the ground.
Lean your chest slightly forward and keep your standing heel down.
Drive back up to standing, then switch legs.
skierg: Stand facing the SkiErg with your feet hip-width apart and grab both handles overhead.
Pull the handles down by hinging at your hips and bending your knees, as if pushing ski poles.
Finish with your hands past your hips.
Let the handles rise as you stand tall again, and keep a steady rhythm.
smith-machine-bulgarian-split-squat: Set the bar at shoulder height and place a bench behind you.
Step under the bar, rest it on your upper back and put the top of your back foot on the bench.
Unhook the bar and lower your back knee toward the floor until your front thigh is about parallel.
Drive through the front heel to stand back up; finish your reps and switch legs.
smith-machine-reverse-lunge: Set the bar at shoulder height, step under it and rest it on your upper back.
Unhook the bar and stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Step one foot back and lower your back knee toward the floor.
Drive through the front heel to bring your foot back, and alternate legs.
sprawl: Drop your hands to the floor and throw your legs back, dropping your hips toward the floor.
Quickly jump your feet back under you.
squat-thrust: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down and place your hands on the floor.
Jump your feet back into a plank, then jump them back to your hands.
step-down: Stand on a box or step on one leg, the other foot hanging just off the edge.
Slowly bend your standing knee to lower the free heel toward the floor.
Tap the floor lightly, keeping your standing knee in line with your toes.
Straighten back up; finish your reps and switch legs.
superman-hold: Lie face down with your arms stretched overhead and legs straight.
Lift your arms, chest and legs a few inches off the floor.
Hold with your neck in line with your spine, looking at the floor.
swimming: Warm up with a few easy lengths.
Swim at a steady pace in the stroke you like, breathing rhythmically.
Keep your body long and near the surface.
Rest at the wall between sets as needed.
toe-touch: Lie on your back with your legs straight up toward the ceiling.
Reach your arms up toward your toes.
Curl your shoulders off the floor to touch or reach toward your toes.
Lower your shoulders slowly and repeat.
torso-twist-stretch: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms relaxed or bent in front of you.
Turn your torso to one side, letting your arms follow.
Turn to the other side in a smooth, controlled rhythm.
Keep your hips fairly still and let the twist come from your upper body.
towel-hamstring-curl: Lie on your back on a smooth floor with your heels on a towel and your knees bent.
Lift your hips into a bridge.
Slide your heels out until your legs are nearly straight, keeping your hips up.
Pull your heels back in to the start.
towel-pull-up: Drape two towels over a sturdy pull-up bar and grab one in each hand.
Pull yourself up as high as you can, squeezing the towels hard.
towel-row: Loop a towel around a sturdy post or closed door handle and hold one end in each hand.
Lean back with straight arms, feet close to the anchor and your body straight.
Pull your chest toward your hands by squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower yourself back slowly. Test the anchor before you start.
treadmill-incline-walk: Set the treadmill to an incline (for example 8 to 12 percent) and a brisk walking pace.
Walk tall, without leaning on or holding the handrails.
Take natural steps and swing your arms.
Keep a steady pace for the set time, then lower the incline to cool down.
typewriter-push-up: Start in a push-up position with your hands wide.
Lower your chest toward one hand.
Keeping low, shift across to the other hand.
Push back up in the middle and repeat in the other direction.
v-up: Lie on your back with your arms overhead and legs straight.
Lift your arms and legs at the same time, reaching your hands toward your feet so your body forms a V.
Balance for a moment at the top.
wall-handstand-push-up: Kick up into a handstand with your back to a wall, hands about shoulder-width apart and a small cushion under your head.
Keep your core tight and legs together against the wall.
Bend your elbows to lower your head toward the floor.
Press back up to straight arms. Build up with pike push-ups first.
wall-push-up: Stand an arm's length from a wall and place your hands on it at shoulder height, a little wider than your shoulders.
Keep your body straight from head to heels.
Bend your elbows to bring your chest toward the wall.
wall-sit: Stand with your back against a wall and your feet about two feet in front of you.
Slide down until your knees are bent at 90 degrees, thighs parallel to the floor.
Keep your back flat against the wall and your knees over your ankles.
wall-walk: Start in a push-up position with your feet against a wall.
Walk your feet up the wall while walking your hands back toward it.
Go as close to the wall as you can control, keeping your body straight.
Walk your hands back out and your feet down to return.
weighted-chin-up: Attach a weight with a dip belt, hold a dumbbell between your feet, or wear a weighted vest.
Grab the bar with your palms facing you, about shoulder-width apart.
Pull yourself up until your chin passes the bar.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
weighted-dip: Attach a weight with a dip belt, or wear a weighted vest.
Support yourself on parallel bars with straight arms.
Lower yourself by bending your elbows until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Press back up to straight arms.
weighted-push-up: Wear a weighted vest, or have a partner place a weight plate on your upper back.
Get into a push-up position with your hands just wider than your shoulders.
Lower your chest toward the floor, keeping your body straight.
Push back up to straight arms.
weighted-russian-twist: Sit on the floor with your knees bent, holding a dumbbell with both hands at your chest.
Lean back slightly with a straight back and lift your feet if you can.
Turn your torso to bring the dumbbell beside one hip.
Turn to the other side and keep alternating.
